description: 3M Consulting shared preset: one run a month, one PR for minor and patch updates, majors only after approval, no version younger than 7 days, nothing merged automatically. The monthly run spans the first three days of the month, for updates and lock file maintenance alike: Mend runs a repository that has not merged a Renovate PR yet only once a day, and the four-hour window of schedule:monthly would be missed most months. Outside those days Renovate leaves its open PRs alone (updateNotScheduled: false): every push to a PR branch costs a CI run on a plan with a monthly minute budget, so a PR that goes into conflict waits for the rebase checkbox or for the next month. Vulnerability PRs ignore the schedule.

packageRules.description: A major is a migration, not an update: its PR opens only after approval in the Dependency Dashboard, and is verified on its own.
In a 0.x package a minor can break as a major does (SemVer; a ^0.8 range does not accept 0.9): it waits for approval in the Dependency Dashboard and gets a PR of its own.

A Python minor (3.12 to 3.13) changes the interpreter, and Python removes deprecated features in minors (PEP 387): it waits for approval like a major, whether it comes from a Docker image, requires-python or setup-python (whose versions come from actions/python-versions).
Patches, pins and digests in one PR: every PR pays for a CI run, and several PRs on the same lock file conflict with each other.
Minors join the same PR, except those of a 0.x package and of Python (rules above).

A version enters 7 days after it was published, whatever the registry: a compromised release is usually found and pulled within days. This replaces the 3 days config:best-practices sets for npm. The package managers apply the same 7 days to what they resolve into the lock file, transitive dependencies included (pnpm minimumReleaseAge, uv exclude-newer). Pins and lock file maintenance are left out: a pin freezes what a reference already points to, and lock file maintenance has no single release date to check.

A new digest for the same Docker tag is a rebuild of the same version (OS patches, a new base). Docker Hub dates it by the last push of the tag, and official images are pushed again every few days: with 7 days they would never update. One day still catches a broken push.

Registries other than Docker Hub (GHCR, GCR, Artifact Registry, Quay, ECR…) publish no release dates: with the default timestamp-required their images would wait for ever, so they move without the age check.

This repository's own workflows and actions are our code: their minor and patch releases join the monthly PR without approval or waiting, so every repository picks up a fix of the shared CI at the next run. A major still waits for approval.
